new_candidates.date_enacted: County Council approved Emergency Ordinance 26-026 on 2026-06-24, effective immediately.
new_candidates.duration: Six-month interim zoning control under RCW 36.70A.390 pausing the filing, acceptance, processing, or approval of applications to establish or expand data centers (including incidental uses) or to change a use to a data center, in all zones of unincorporated Snohomish County. Requires a public hearing within 60 days and permits six-month renewals after hearing and findings.
new_candidates.legal_basis: Emergency Ordinance 26-026; RCW 36.70A.390 interim zoning control
new_candidates.trigger: Covers data centers with a total planned electrical load of at least 2 MW; adopted while the county develops permanent regulations.
new_candidates.current_status: Active as of 2026-07-31; six-month interim control effective 2026-06-24, renewable in six-month increments after hearing and findings.

evidence.supports: Adopted text of Emergency Ordinance 26-026 establishing the six-month data center moratorium

new_candidates.date_enacted: City Council adopted Ordinance 905 by a 6-0 vote on 2026-06-29, effective immediately.
new_candidates.duration: One-year moratorium in all city districts on accepting, processing, or approving applications to establish, expand, or change a use to a data center with capacity exceeding 20 MVA. Preserves vested rights for complete permit applications filed before the effective date. Public hearing scheduled for 2026-07-13.
new_candidates.current_status: Active as of 2026-07-31; one-year moratorium effective 2026-06-29.

new_candidates.date_enacted: City Council unanimously adopted Ordinance No. 3381 on 2026-07-13.
new_candidates.duration: Six-month pause on acceptance, processing, and approval of land-use and permit applications for facilities whose principal use is digital-data processing, storage, management, or transmission; incidental server equipment supporting another principal use is excluded. Public hearing required within 60 days.

new_candidates.trigger: Study period covers siting, public safety, land-use compatibility, water and sewer planning, utility rates, and permanent code amendments.
